questionText:

questionText:
Direction: The following question consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence which is split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named as P, Q, R and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

While the recent ______.

P : century show that the June rainfall is

Q : of a drought, India's rainfall data for over a

R : rain may have soothed concerns

S : no predictor of the monsoon's outcome
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'RQPS.'

Key Points

  • While arranging the parts of the sentence given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let's find out.
  • In this sentence, we can see that there are different parts like Subject, verb, conjunction and continuation of the object.
  • The first part should be R as it is providing sense to the first part of the sentence with the help of the part "rain may have soothed."
  • R should be followed by Q as a complete sense to the part R is provided with the help of the preposition "of."
  • Q should be followed by P as the phrase "over a" is completed with the help of the word "century."
  • The last part should be S as S is talking about a prediction of the monsoon's outcome.
  • Thus, forming the basic structure of a sentence.
  • ​​Correct sentence: While the recent rain may have soothed concerns of a drought, India's rainfall data for over a century show that the June rainfall is no predictor of the monsoon's outcome.

Additional Information

  • Before rearranging parts of the sentence, it is very important to read them carefully.
  • It is very important to analyse the use of a determiner and conjunction in such cases.
  • This confusion can be eradicated by practising more and more questions of Sentence Jumbles.

Hinglish

  • विकल्पों में दिए गए वाक्य के भागों को व्यवस्थित करते समय हमें उनके बीच कुछ व्याकरणिक या प्रासंगिक संबंध खोजने होंगे, तो आइए जानें।
  • इस वाक्य में, हम देख सकते हैं कि Subject, verb, conjunction and continuation of the object जैसे विभिन्न भाग हैं।
  • पहला भाग R होना चाहिए क्योंकि यह वाक्य के पहले भाग को part "rain may have soothed" की मदद से अर्थ प्रदान कर रहा है।
  • R के बाद Q का पालन किया जाना चाहिए क्योंकि भाग R को पूर्ण अर्थ के रूप में preposition "of" की सहायता से प्रदान किया जाता है।
  • Q के बाद P आना चाहिए क्योंकि phrase "over a", word "century" की मदद से पूरा होता है।
  • अंतिम भाग S होना चाहिए क्योंकि S मानसून के परिणाम की भविष्यवाणी के बारे में बात कर रहा है।
  • इस प्रकार, एक वाक्य की मूल संरचना का निर्माण हैं।

questionText:

questionText:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'

One of the (A) / files in the cabinet (B) / are missing. (C) / No error (D)
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. C.

  • The given sentence is starting with the phrase "one of the".
  • The noun following the phrase "one of the" is always a plural noun i.e. 'files' in the given sentence.
  • The verb following the phrase "one of the" is always singular as the subject 'one' is singular.
  • For example:
    • ​One of the girls is doing homework.
  • Therefore, the plural verb 'are' should be replaced by 'is' in the given sentence.
  • Hence, the phrase "are missing" contains an error.

​ The correct sentence: "One of the files in the cabinet is missing."

questionText:

questionText:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no improvement required, select 'No improvement'.

Scarcely he see his opponent than he went numb with fear.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'No sooner did' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the phrase 'Scarcely he see' is incorrect.
  • The correct expression is 'No sooner did he see' as it follows the correct grammatical structure for such sentences.
  • The structure for such sentences is: No sooner + did + subject + base form of the verb + than.
    • Example: No sooner did she arrive than it started raining.
  • Therefore, the correct form should be 'No sooner did he see'.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: No sooner did he see his opponent than he went numb with fear.

Additional Information

  • The phrases 'No sooner... than' and 'Hardly... when' are often used to indicate that one action quickly followed another.
    • Example: Hardly had he arrived when the meeting started.
  • These phrases are used with the past perfect or simple past tense, and the auxiliary verb (did/had) is used before the subject.

questionText:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

He is faster enough / to defeat / the current record holder.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'He is faster enough'.

Key Points

  • The question involves identifying a grammatical error in the given sentence.
  • The sentence is divided into parts, and we need to find the part that is grammatically incorrect.
  • The first part of the sentence says 'He is faster enough', which is not grammatically correct.
  • In English, we usually say someone is "fast enough" or "quick enough", not "faster enough".
  • The adverb 'enough' modifies adjectives but it does not usually modify comparatives.
  • So, the error lies in the first part of the sentence.
  • 'To defeat' and 'the current record holder' are grammatically correct as they convey clear and specific meanings.
  • 'To defeat' indicates the action that can be done because the person is 'fast enough', and 'The current record holder' identifies who the person can defeat.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

questionText:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. and allows them to come out of their imaginary world

Q. which helps in illuminating and enlightening the dark world

R. of two blind or visually impaired persons

S. eye donation is a very generous act towards society
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is 'SQRP'.

Key Points

  • The correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence is SQRP, which reads as "Eye donation is a very generous act towards society, which helps in illuminating and enlightening the dark world of two blind or visually impaired persons and allows them to come out of their imaginary world."
  • Option 4 starts with S, introducing the topic of eye donation.
  • It is logically followed by Q, which explains the impact of this act.
  • Then comes R, specifying the beneficiaries of the act.
  • Finally, P concludes the sentence by explaining the outcome for those beneficiaries.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: Eye donation is a very generous act towards society, which helps in illuminating and enlightening the dark world of two blind or visually impaired persons and allows them to come out of their imaginary world.

Additional Information

  • Option 1 (SQPR): This option incorrectly places "R" at the end, disrupting the logical flow of beneficiaries before the outcome.
  • Option 2 (SRQP): This sequence incorrectly suggests that the sentence starts with the beneficiaries, which is illogical as an introduction to the act of eye donation.
  • Option 3 (SPQR): This order places the outcome before explaining who benefits, which makes the sentence confusing.

questionText:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The captain dropped the trophy while he ________the victory with his teammates.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.
Key Points
  • The sentence requires the past continuous tense to indicate an action that was ongoing at the time another action occurred.
  • The past continuous tense is formed using "was/were" + the present participle (verb + -ing).
  • In this case, "was celebrating" correctly indicates that the celebration was in progress when the trophy was dropped.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
Correct Sentence: "The captain dropped the trophy while he was celebrating the victory with his teammates."
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "celebrated" – This is the simple past tense, which does not convey the ongoing nature of the action.
  • Option 3: "is celebrating" – This is the present continuous tense, which is not appropriate for past events.
  • Option 4: "celebrates" – This is the simple present tense, which is not appropriate for past events.

questionText:
The following question consists of an incomplete sentence or a sentence that is split into four parts. All four parts are jumbled up and are named P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Arrange the jumbled parts of the sentence and find out which of the four combinations from the given options will correctly complete the sentence.

Gujarat is a classic example of learning______________________

P: acquired the hard way with

Q: every reason to share the expertise

R: to cope with disasters, and there is

S: other Indian states and other nations.
solutionExplanation:
The correct answer is “RQPS”

Key Points

This paragraph talks about the 'Gujarat is a classic example of learning how to deal with disasters.'

  • If we read the opening statement clearly, we can conclude that the next statement should continue to explain what learning is about.
    • Clause 'R' performs this, and it is established that clause 'R' is the following fragment. Thus, the introductory clause and clause 'R' form a mandatory pair.
  • Further, clause 'R' ends with 'is' and clause 'Q' begins with singular 'every reason.' Thus, clause 'R' and clause 'Q' also form a mandatory pair.
  • Clause 'P' is dependent on clause 'Q' as it continues “… share the expertise… acquired the hard way…'

Hence, the correct answer is “Gujarat is a classic example of learning to cope with disasters, and there is every reason to share the expertise acquired the hard way with other Indian states and other nations.”

Additional Information

When we are doing Sentence Rearrangement & Para jumbles, we have to keep three things in our mind:

  1. Identify the introductory and concluding sentences.
  2. After identifying the first and last sentences, the next task is to trace the flow of information the author used. By doing this, you will be able to see the purpose of all the paragraphs, which by default will prompt you to develop a sequence between the sentences.
  3. 'For solving parajumbles, combining statements based on particular characteristics or indicators works well.

questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below.   • Given below are the points, we should keep in mind while solving questions of reading passage-
    • Identify the purpose of the passage.
    • Anticipate what may lie ahead.
    • Try to go through the question first then the passage so that you can just focus on the things you need to look in the passage.
    • Read the passage quickly to get a general idea of meaning or to find specific information, e.g. figures or names.

questionText:
Direction: Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow. A papal decree of 1493 had assigned all land in the New World west of 50 degrees W longitude to Spain and all the land east of that line to Portugal. Magellan offered to prove that the East Indies fell under Spanish authority. On September 20, 1519, Magellan set sail from Spain with five ships. More than a year later, one of these ships was exploring the topography of South America in search of a water route across the continent. Directions: Read the following passage and answer the questions accordingly. India and Russia deepened their strategic partnership on Friday by signing nine pacts, including a multi-billion dollar deal for New Delhi to buy the S-400 Triumf air defense missile system despite warnings from the United States that the move could attract sanctions on India under American domestic law. A joint statement issued after talks between visiting Russian President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Narendra Modi confirmed the $ 5.4 billion deal, though neither leader referred to it in their remarks to reporters. Another expected defense pact on India acquiring four frigates from Russia was not signed as the two sides were yet to agree on some issues. Putin arrived in New Delhi on Thursday to a red carpet welcome, on a day when the US, Britain, and the Netherlands accused Russia of involvement in a series of cyber plots across the globe, adding to tensions between Moscow and Western nations on a host of issues. India's move to acquire the S-400, which has the ability to track multiple incoming targets, including aircraft, missiles, and unmanned aerial vehicles, up to 400km in distance and 30km in altitude, can attract sanctions under the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (Caatsa) passed by the US Congress on arms purchases from Russia. The US embassy in New Delhi said on Friday that Caatsa was not aimed at stymieing the military capabilities of its “allies or partners", a statement is seen in New Delhi as indicative of a possible waiver coming through from Washington. Waivers of the Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (Caatsa) section 231 will be considered on a transaction-by-transaction basis. We cannot prejudge any sanctions decisions, the US embassy spokesperson in New Delhi said. “The intent of our implementation of Caatsa is to impose costs on Russia for its malign behavior, including by stopping the flow of money to Russia's defense sector," the embassy said. On the waiver itself, it said: “The waiver authority is not for a blanket waiver. It is transaction-specific. There are strict criteria for considering a waiver." To put economic ties on a stronger footing, Russia has evinced interest in collaboration in the railways and civilian aircraft manufacturing sectors, a person familiar with the development said. India on its part is keen for its pharmaceutical companies to find a foothold in Russian markets, the person said. Both sides have set the target for increasing bilateral trade to $30 billion by 2025 from $10.7 billion in 2017-18. India “invited Russian companies to participate in the development of industrial corridors in India, including in areas of road and rail infrastructure, smart cities, construction of wagons and creation of a joint transportation logistics company," according to the statement.
